neighbours.label: the pivot right after merit is conceded, where a 'falls short / does not go far enough' verdict is coming ('… is welcome but ▁stops short of', 'While … is a good start, ▁it …'); the pole's output promotes fall/falls
fire: The new law is a step in the right direction but stops short of banning the pesticide outright.
The apology was sincere but stops short of admitting any legal responsibility.
While the treaty is an encouraging start, it needs to go much further to protect the reefs.
The report praises the reforms but stops short of recommending more funding.
Although the settlement is a welcome first step, it falls short of what the families asked for.
The ruling is a victory for tenants but stops short of capping rents.
While the pledge is a fine beginning, it does not go nearly far enough to cut emissions.
The plan moves in the right direction but stops short of a full ban on logging.
quiet: The new law is a step in the right direction and bans the pesticide outright.
The apology was sincere and admits full legal responsibility.
While the treaty was being signed, it rained heavily over the harbour.
The report praises the reforms and recommends more funding.
Although the settlement took years, it gives the families everything they asked for.
The ruling is a victory for tenants and caps rents for five years.
While the pledge was being drafted, it was leaked to the newspapers.
The plan covers the whole forest and includes a full ban on logging.

notes: Card: ' short' x7, ' it' x4, ' stops', ' fallen' in 'stops short of', 'a terrific start, it needs to go farther'; logit effect (- pole) promotes fall/falls/falling. Probes: 'welcome but stops (short)' 0.75, 'a good start, it' 0.38, 'shortfalls' 0.21; but plain 'has fallen short of expectations' 0.03, 'a short walk' 0.01, so it is the concession-then-shortfall context, not the word 'short'.
